html:
The Gooniyandi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern Kimberley in Western Australia, around the Margaret River and the Fitzroy River near Fitzroy Crossing. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their language, Gooniyandi, is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia; it is related to the language of their neighbours the Bunuba. Other neighbours were the Walmajarri of the desert to the south and the Jaru to the east.

Cattle stations took over the Fitzroy valley from the 1880s, and many Gooniyandi worked on them for rations rather than wages. When equal pay came to the stations in the late 1960s, many were pushed off and moved into Fitzroy Crossing, where most live today.
sum: The Gooniyandi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southern Kimberley in Western Australia, around the Margaret River and the Fitzroy River near Fitzroy Crossing. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.
